name: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes
overview: National fine arts museum in Recoleta, Buenos Aires (Spanish Wikipedia).

Created by decree of President José Evaristo Uriburu in 1895 with Eduardo Schiaffino as first director. It opened on 25 December 1896 in the Bon Marché building on calle Florida with 163 works (Spanish Wikipedia).
Its permanent home is the former Casa de Bombas, a pumping station in Recoleta, redesigned by the architect Alejandro Bustillo (Spanish Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes: national state museum, with a private Friends association

name: Sydney Symphony Orchestra
overview: Sydney Symphony Orchestra, run by Sydney Symphony Limited, plays in the Concert Hall and Utzon Room at the Sydney Opera House; its office is at Level 17, 56 Pitt Street (orchestra website).
The pages read did not state when it was founded. 2023 was the second year of Simone Young AM's tenure as Chief Conductor (financial report 2023).
What is there: an orchestra and concert seasons; the site advertises 2027 season tickets.
funding_verdict: Sydney Symphony Orchestra: mixed, federal and NSW grants plus tickets and donors

name: Proyecto mARTadero
overview: Social development and arts project on Calle 27 de Agosto y Ollantay in the Villa Coronilla neighbourhood of Cochabamba, a few blocks from the city centre, an area long seen as peripheral because of the slaughterhouse, rural migration and its image as a "red zone" (mARTadero, "Historia").

Housed in the former municipal slaughterhouse, built in 1924 and awaiting heritage listing as early 20th century industrial architecture; the site is about 2,900 to 3,000 square metres (mARTadero, "Quienes somos" and "Historia").
After 1992 the building served in turn as a makeshift school, a sports space and a depot for public lighting, unused municipal furniture and scrap, and it fell into decay (mARTadero, "Historia").
funding_verdict: Proyecto mARTadero: supporter-funded: Misereor and Oxfam listed as current supporters, in a municipal building held on a 30-year concession

name: National Gallery (Sofia)
overview: Bulgaria's national art museum, 'a state cultural and scientific institution of national importance', with its permanent display in Kvadrat 500 on St Alexander Nevsky Square, Sofia, and temporary exhibitions in the Palace at 1, Knyaz Alexander I Sq. (gallery website).

The gallery was established in 1948; Kvadrat 500, designed by Yanko Apostolov after a 2010 competition, joins the 1881 to 1883 State Printing House to the former National Gallery of Foreign Art and opened to the public on 25 May 2015 (gallery website).

The collection holds more than 42,000 pieces, of which Kvadrat 500 shows about 1,700 in 28 halls: Christian art from the Bulgarian lands of the 4th to 19th centuries, Bulgarian art of the 19th and 20th centuries, European art of the 15th to 20th centuries, art from Asia, Africa and America, 21st-century art and a graphics collection (gallery website). The gallery bought a work by Christo and Jeanne-Claude about a year before December 2025 (BTA, 9 December 2025).
funding_verdict: National Gallery: public, Bulgarian state subsidy plus ticket income

name: Centro Cultural La Moneda
aliases: Centro Cultural Palacio de La Moneda
Fundación Centro Cultural Palacio de La Moneda
overview: Centro Cultural La Moneda is at Plaza de la Ciudadanía 26, Santiago, run by the Fundación Centro Cultural Palacio de La Moneda (museum website; financial statements).
The pages read did not state who founded it or when it opened.

What is there: exhibition halls open Tuesday to Sunday 10:15 to 18:45; the 2025 statements record revenue lines for a Cineteca and its laboratory, a shop, concessions and rural programme 'Mundo rural'. The pages read gave no object count.
funding_verdict: Centro Cultural La Moneda: mainly public, through the Ministry of Cultures, with earned income

name: Capital Museum
overview: The Capital Museum (首都博物馆) describes itself as a large, comprehensive city museum of local history belonging to Beijing municipality, and a national first-grade museum (museum website, our translation of 北京市属大型地志类综合性城市博物馆).
Planned from 1953, it opened in 1981 in the Beijing Confucius Temple (Visit Beijing, the city's tourism site).

Its present building at 16 Fuxingmenwai Dajie, Xicheng District (复兴门外大街16号), has 64,000 square metres of floor space and opened on 18 May 2006 (museum website); Chinese Wikipedia places it on the former site of the First Ministry of Machine Building's automobile bureau.
funding_verdict: Capital Museum: public: a Beijing city institution under the Beijing Municipal Cultural Heritage Bureau

name: National Art Museum of China
overview: China's national art museum, at 1 Wusi Street, Dongcheng District, Beijing.

Built from November 1958. The main building was finished on 15 November 1961. It was first called the China Art Exhibition Hall, and in June 1963 Mao Zedong chose the name China National Art Museum (Chinese Wikipedia, in translation). It opened to the public in 1963 (Beijing municipal government).

Building: designed by the architect Dai Nianci in a traditional Chinese pavilion style with yellow glazed tiles. The main building covers more than 18,000 square metres, with 6,660 square metres of exhibition space in 21 halls (Beijing municipal government; Chinese Wikipedia gives 22,379 square metres of floor area).
funding_verdict: National Art Museum of China: mainly public: the Chinese state, through the Ministry of Culture and Tourism

name: Guangdong Museum
overview: The provincial museum of Guangdong at 2 Zhujiang East Road, in the Cultural and Art Square of Zhujiang New Town, Tianhe District, on Guangzhou's new central axis (China Daily).

A preparatory committee was formed on 19 July 1957, and the museum and the Guangzhou Lu Xun Memorial Hall opened on 1 October 1959 on Wenming Road, on the site of the old Guangdong examination hall (China Daily; Chinese Wikipedia).

In 2003 the provincial government decided to build a new museum and held an invited international design competition; Rocco Design of Hong Kong won among ten firms from eight countries, building began on 12 December 2004 and the new museum opened on 18 May 2010 (Chinese Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Guangdong Museum: public: the Guangdong provincial budget, through the provincial culture department

name: Zhejiang Museum
overview: The Zhejiang Provincial Museum (浙江省博物馆) is the largest comprehensive museum in Zhejiang and one of the first national first-grade museums (The Paper, 2023).

Founded in 1929 as the Zhejiang Provincial West Lake Museum (The Paper, 2023; Travel China Guide); Chinese Wikipedia states the provincial government set it up to keep objects from the West Lake Expo.

It now has two main sites: the Gushan (Solitary Hill) site by West Lake, rebuilt in 1993 (Hangzhou News, 2019), and the Zhijiang site in the new Zhijiang Cultural Center, opened on 29 August 2023; a Wulin site on West Lake Cultural Square opened in 2009 (The Paper, 2023; Travel China Guide).
funding_verdict: Zhejiang Museum: public: Zhejiang provincial government, with central government co-funding

name: Hubei Provincial Museum
overview: The Hubei Provincial Museum is at 160 Donghu Road, Wuchang, Wuhan, founded in 1953 and at its East Lake site since 1960 (World Museum Guide).
The pages read do not name its founder or operating body.

What is there: 16 pieces or sets of state-level treasures, among them the Sword of Goujian (unearthed 1965 at Wangshan, Jingzhou), the chime bells from the tomb of Marquis Yi of Zeng (excavated 1978 at Suizhou; 65 bronze bells), the Yunxian Man skull fossils and the Qin bamboo slips from Shuihudi (found 1975) (Wuhan government page; World Museum Guide). The pages give no total count.
funding_verdict: Hubei Provincial Museum: the pages read name no funder; free standard entry

name: Statens Museum for Kunst (SMK)
overview: Denmark's national gallery, a state institution under the Ministry of Culture, in Vilhelm Dahlerup's building on Sølvgade in Copenhagen, with an extension by Anna Maria Indrio built from 1993 to 1998, and a branch, SMK Thy, at Doverodde Købmandsgård (Lex.dk; museum website).

The core of the collection was separated from the royal Kunstkammer in 1824 and shown in the Royal Picture Gallery at Christiansborg from 1827; it passed to the state when democracy was introduced, in 1848 by Lex.dk's account and 1849 by the museum's, and the Sølvgade building opened in 1896 (Lex.dk; museum website).

What is there: more than 200,000 Danish and foreign paintings, sculptures, prints and drawings from the 1300s to today, begun with the Danish kings' purchases in the 1500s; older European art with Cranach, Mantegna, Titian and Rembrandt, the Danish Golden Age, the largest holdings of Christen Købke and Vilhelm Hammershøi by the museum's account, and French modernism from engineer Johannes Rump's gift of 1927, which included 25 works by Matisse. Lex.dk counts about 8,500 paintings and sculptures and about 300,000 works in the Royal Collection of Graphic Art; the museum's study room page gives more than 240,000 works on paper (museum website; Lex.dk).
funding_verdict: Statens Museum for Kunst: a little over half state appropriation, the rest ticket and shop sales and foundation grants
wider_context: Denmark's colonial past touches the museum in two documented ways: its cast collection is housed in the West India Warehouse, where guided tours cover the building's part in Denmark's transnational slave trade (museum website), and in 2017, the centenary of the sale of the three West Indian islands to the USA, it mounted the display What Lies Unspoken with the Royal Library to read works by Eckersberg, Abildgaard, Juel and Astrid Holm from the standpoint of enslaved people, which the museum said earlier studies had overlooked (Meer).

name: Les Rencontres d'Arles
overview: Annual summer festival of photography in Arles, with more than forty exhibitions in heritage sites of the town; offices at 34 rue du docteur Fanton (festival website).
Founded in 1970; the 57th edition ran from 6 July to 4 October 2026 (festival website; Objectif Gard, July 2026).

What is there: exhibitions of historical and contemporary photography, the Prix Découverte Fondation Louis Roederer, the Arles Books fair, photography workshops and a portfolio review, and education programmes; the festival also lists a collection on its site (festival website).
funding_verdict: Les Rencontres d'Arles: about 70 % own income, patrons and tickets; public grants for the rest

name: Palais des Beaux-Arts de Lille
overview: Municipal fine arts museum on place de la République in Lille, in a palace by the architects Bérard and Delmas with a glass 'blade' building added behind it in 1997 (museum website).

The Palais was inaugurated on 6 March 1892; the city financed it by a lottery of five million one-franc tickets that brought in half the hoped-for sum, so the plans were cut. Requisitioned by the German army in October 1914 and hit by more than seventy shells, it reopened in 1924. After two years of closure the renovated museum, by Jean-Marc Ibos and Myrto Vitart, was inaugurated on 8 June 1997 and grew from 15,000 to 22,000 m2 (museum website).

What is there: more than 1,300 paintings, among them Goya's Les Jeunes and Les Vieilles, bought in 1873, with works by David, Delacroix, Courbet, Monet and Rodin; a graphic arts cabinet built on Jean-Baptiste Wicar's bequest of nearly 1,300 drawings, including Raphael's study for the Alba Madonna; antiquities, medieval and Renaissance works; and relief maps of fortified towns of northern Europe at 1:600 (14 by Le Quotidien de l'Art's count, sixteen by the museum's history page), shown under the atrium since 1997 and restored between April 2018 and March 2019 (museum website; scientific and cultural project; Le Quotidien de l'Art, 18 March 2019).
funding_verdict: Palais des Beaux-Arts de Lille: municipal, the City of Lille pays; tickets, grants and regional patrons add income

name: La Friche la Belle de Mai
overview: Cultural complex in the Belle de Mai neighbourhood of Marseille, in a former tobacco factory of the SEITA. The site says it has been converted into a cultural venue since 1992 (lafriche.org, French page).
Run since 2007 by a Société Coopérative d'Intérêt Collectif (SCIC) with variable capital (lafriche.org, French page).
Named for its neighbourhood, Belle de Mai (lafriche.org).
funding_verdict: La Friche la Belle de Mai: public support: the State, Région Sud, the Bouches-du-Rhône département and the City of Marseille

name: Musée Fabre
aliases: Musée Fabre de Montpellier Méditerranée Métropole
overview: Fine arts museum on boulevard Bonne Nouvelle in Montpellier, with a decorative arts department in the Hôtel de Cabrières-Sabatier d'Espeyran; a large renovation was completed in 2007 (museum website).

Founded in 1825 by the painter François-Xavier Fabre (1766-1837), after a first museum of the Revolution years and the Société des Beaux-Arts de Montpellier of 1779; open to the public since 1828 (museum website; France 3 Occitanie, January 2025).

What is there: Flemish and Dutch painting from Fabre's gifts and the bequest of the stockbroker Antoine Valedau (1777-1836); 19th century French painting given mostly by Alfred Bruyas (1821-1877), including Courbet's La Rencontre and Les Baigneuses; works by the Montpellier painters Alexandre Cabanel and Frédéric Bazille; a group of works by Pierre Soulages; and 18th century Montpellier silver (museum website). The pages read did not give a total number of works.
funding_verdict: Musée Fabre: public, Montpellier's local authorities; a company foundation funds acquisitions

name: Musée d'arts de Nantes
overview: Fine arts museum at 10 rue Georges Clemenceau in central Nantes, formerly the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Nantes; a musée de France since 5 January 2002 (Museofile record; Le Voyage à Nantes).

Founding: the Museofile record dates the consular order creating the museum to 1800; Apollo dates the Chaptal decree to 1801, and Le Voyage à Nantes also gives 1801. The City bought the Cacault collection in 1810, the works went on show in the Halle aux toiles in 1830, and a new palace by the Nantes-born architect Clément-Marie Josso opened in 1900 (Museofile record; Apollo, 26 June 2017).
The seventeenth-century Chapelle de l'Oratoire was restored and given to the museum in 1988 (Apollo).
funding_verdict: Musée d'arts de Nantes: public: Nantes Métropole, with 2017 renovation money from the EU, the State, the Region, the Département and the City

name: Cité de l'architecture et du patrimoine
aliases: Cité de l'architecture et du patrimoine (Palais de Chaillot)
overview: The Cité de l'architecture et du patrimoine is at the Palais de Chaillot, Place du Trocadéro, and is part of the Ministry of Culture (institution's website).
The pages read do not give a founding date.

What is there: the Cast Gallery of the Musée des Monuments français, a Modern and Contemporary Architecture Gallery and a Murals and Stained Glass Gallery (institution's website). The 2021 report counts 4,000 architectural casts and 350 reproductions of murals.
funding_verdict: Cité de l'architecture et du patrimoine: mainly public, State grant with about one sixth own income

name: Musée d'Art Moderne de Paris
aliases: Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris
overview: The City of Paris's museum of 20th and 21st century art at 11, avenue du Président-Wilson, in a building made for the Exposition internationale des arts et des techniques of 1937 (Paris Musées annual report 2025).

It was inaugurated in 1961, an opening made possible by the bequest of 533 works from the dealer Maurice Girardin, reopened after renovation in 2019 and has been run by Paris Musées since 2013 (Paris Musées annual report 2025; The Art Newspaper, 13 June 2025).

The collection holds close to 16 000 works covering fauvism, cubism, the École de Paris, abstraction, nouveau réalisme, figuration narrative and conceptual art, with two works made for the site, Raoul Dufy's La Fée Électricité and Matisse's La Danse; it has received over 800 works since 2007, including gifts from the estates of Josef Albers and Zao Wou-Ki and Michael Werner's gift of 127 works in 2012 (Paris Musées annual report 2025; The Art Newspaper, 13 June 2025).
funding_verdict: Musée d'Art Moderne de Paris: mainly public, paid by the City of Paris through Paris Musées, with corporate exhibition patrons and dealer gifts

name: Musée de l'Orangerie
aliases: Établissement public du musée d'Orsay et du musée de l'Orangerie
overview: National museum in the former orangery of the Tuileries garden, on the Seine side of place de la Concorde, Paris (museum website).

Claude Monet offered the Nymphéas to France the day after the armistice of 11 November 1918; they were installed to his plans in 1927, a few months after his death. Since 2010 the museum has formed one public establishment with the Musée d'Orsay (museum website; EPMO website).

What is there: Monet's Nymphéas cycle, and the Jean Walter and Paul Guillaume collection of 148 works from the 1860s to the 1930s: 25 Renoir, 15 Cézanne, 12 Picasso, 10 Matisse, 5 Modigliani, 9 Douanier Rousseau, 30 Derain, 22 Soutine, 10 Utrillo, 6 Marie Laurencin. The dealer Paul Guillaume formed it between 1914 and his death in 1934; his widow Domenica, remarried to the architect and industrialist Jean Walter, 'transformed and reduced' it and made new purchases; the state acquired it in 1959 and 1963 subject to her life interest, and she kept the pictures until 1977 (museum website).
funding_verdict: Musée de l'Orangerie: public establishment shared with Orsay, about three fifths self-earned, the rest a state grant

name: Berliner Festspiele
aliases: Kulturveranstaltungen des Bundes in Berlin GmbH
overview: Berliner Festspiele organises festivals, exhibitions, concerts, dance and theatre through the year, in the Haus der Berliner Festspiele at Schaperstraße 24 and the Gropius Bau at Niederkirchnerstraße 7 (Berliner Festspiele website).

The Berliner Festwochen were started in 1951, in the same year as the Berlin film festival; under the capital culture treaty the federal government became sole shareholder of Berliner Festspiele GmbH in 2001, and KBB was formed with effect from 1 January 2002 by merger with Haus der Kulturen der Welt GmbH (KBB website, history page). The institution marks its 75th anniversary in 2026 (Berliner Festspiele website).

What is there: the Haus der Berliner Festspiele, built by Fritz Bornemann and opened on 1 May 1963 as the Theater der Freien Volksbühne, a 1,000-seat theatre the Festspiele moved into in December 2000 and reopened on 21 April 2001; the programme is Theatertreffen, Musikfest Berlin, MaerzMusik, Jazzfest Berlin, the Performing Arts Season, Reflexe und Reflexionen and the youth contests of Treffen junge Szene (Berliner Festspiele website).
funding_verdict: Berliner Festspiele: public, a division of a federal company

name: Flutgraben
overview: Self-organised, non-profit artists' studio house at Am Flutgraben 3, 12435 Berlin, on the Treptow side of the Flutgraben canal that separates Kreuzberg and Treptow (visitBerlin, Flutgraben).

The association was founded in 1997 as "Kunstfabrik am Flutgraben" and runs the house as Flutgraben e.V. (Flutgraben). Since 2004 it has also managed the former watch tower at Schlesischer Busch, which the initiative The Watch uses for exhibitions, lectures, screenings and residencies (Flutgraben).

The building is a former workshop of VEB OLW in brick, on the border with West Berlin. The Berlin State Monuments Office calls it the only East Berlin border house that survived the expansion of the border fortifications. Roof catwalks were built in 1988, and the 1990s facade renovation preserved traces of the border (Landesdenkmalamt).
funding_verdict: Flutgraben: self-funded: studio rents and room hire

press_items.title: Ingeborg Ruthe, "Herrscht etwa Darwinismus im Atelierhaus Flutgraben e.V.?" (8 December 2023)

name: Gropius Bau
overview: Exhibition house for large temporary exhibitions at 7 Niederkirchnerstrasse in Berlin-Kreuzberg (Wikipedia).
Built from 1877 to 1881 in neo-Renaissance style by the architects Martin Gropius and Heino Schmieden, and named for Gropius. It first housed the Museum of Applied Arts (Wikipedia).

Heavily damaged in 1945. The German Wikipedia says the Berlin Wall stood directly in front of the main entrance from 1961 to 1989. Declared a historic monument in 1966, rebuilt from 1978, and reopened in 1981 with a Schinkel exhibition (Wikipedia, German Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Gropius Bau: mainly public: German federal government through the Berliner Festspiele, with money raised per exhibition
